ADU218 whole-port write (MKddd) witnessed by an instrument
==========================================================
Device: Ontrak ADU218, USB 0a07:00da, s/n E02246
Witness: SDM4065A s/n SDM46A0CA00021, 2-wire resistance, on K7
Wiring: K7 contact -> DMM leads only. No load current. Standing DC
        0.0006 V, so the leads are on a dry contact and not a rail.
Captured: 2026-08-27, at commit 90e18f5 (the witnessed test) + 0145271

Why this capture exists
-----------------------
The two whole-port mask writes in the gated all-eight sweep were checked
only against relay_mask() -- the device reporting on itself. A firmware
that accepted MKddd, updated its own state word and never moved a
contact satisfied that check completely. The per-relay SKn/RKn path has
had a DMM witness since the first bench session (switch_k0.txt); this
path had none.

The bench has ONE meter, which looked like the reason it could not be
witnessed. It is not: the sweep's two masks are COMPLEMENTS, so
whichever relay the meter is across, one mask closes it and the other
opens it.

  0b10101010 ^ 0b01010101 = 0b11111111

With TEST_RELAY = 7 (the leading bit), MK170 closes K7 and MK085 opens
it. One relay of eight is still all this witnesses -- but it is the same
code path for all eight, and it is the difference between "the command
path is asserted" and "the command path is measured".

Readings
--------
Three passes of the exact sequence the test performs. reset_relays()
first, so the run starts from a known safe state rather than assuming
one.

  step                  mask         bit7   DMM
  -------------------   ----------   ----   ---------------------
  reset_relays          0b00000000     -    OPEN (overload)
  set_relay_port MK170  0b10101010     1    CLOSED  17.5134 ohm
  set_relay_port MK085  0b01010101     0    OPEN (overload)

  reset_relays          0b00000000     -    OPEN (overload)
  set_relay_port MK170  0b10101010     1    CLOSED  17.5147 ohm
  set_relay_port MK085  0b01010101     0    OPEN (overload)

  reset_relays          0b00000000     -    OPEN (overload)
  set_relay_port MK170  0b10101010     1    CLOSED  17.5152 ohm
  set_relay_port MK085  0b01010101     0    OPEN (overload)

  final reset_relays    0b00000000     -    OPEN (overload)
  left on the device: relay mask 0b00000000, WD 0

Every set_relay_port() call also returned the mask it was given, i.e.
the device's own PK read-back agreed -- but that agreement is exactly
what cannot be trusted alone, and is not what this file records.

Two things the numbers add that the assertions cannot
----------------------------------------------------
1. MK085 is the reading that carries the information. It OPENS the
   metered relay while closing seven others, which is what a
   state-word-only bug cannot fake: it has to open a contact the driver
   never named individually, on the strength of a bit position inside a
   three-digit decimal argument. Getting that endianness backwards is
   the plausible defect, and it lands here.

2. The closed reading matches the OTHER command path. The bench walk
   measured K7 at 17.50 ohm through the per-relay SKn route (F-27's
   eight-relay table). MKddd puts the same contact at 17.5134-17.5152
   ohm, spread 0.0018 ohm across three passes. Two independent command
   paths, one contact, the same resistance -- so MKddd is closing the
   relay the same way SKn does, not by some other route that merely
   ends up reported as closed.

Deliberately NOT asserted
-------------------------
The committed test asserts CATEGORICALLY -- finite vs the overload
sentinel -- and must keep doing so. Per F-27 the closed reading is a
property of the WIRING, not the relay: K0 read 9.483 ohm and K7 reads
~17.5 ohm on identical PhotoMOS parts (vendor maximum 1.1 ohm, so the
relay is under 7% of even this reading). A 17.5 ohm expectation would
fail the moment the leads move. The corroboration above is a fact about
this bench on this day, which is why it lives in a fixture and not in
an assertion.

Contact-to-contact SKEW inside one MKddd remains unmeasured, and only
one relay of the eight is metered. See MEGAPLAN_ADU218.md §19 for why
the skew claim is not worth an instrument (the manual gives no
per-relay switching time, so there would be nothing to pass or fail)
and §20 for this capture.
